commentary: Sweden's 2024 GDP growth of 0.82% — recovering from a -0.2% contraction in 2023 — provides modest economic tailwinds for the housing market reforms voted in this batch of committee reports. Sweden's rate lags Denmark's 3.5% growth and Norway's 2.1%, underscoring why policy reforms targeting the housing sector carry particular electoral weight: in a slow-growth economy, property wealth represents a disproportionate share of household balance sheets, making anti-fraud housing legislation and market transparency measures politically salient ahead of the September 2026 election.
